title: Computational investigation of covalent organic pyrgos[n]cages as potential dual modulators of the VEGFR-2 D2-D3 domain and DNA structural interfaces.
one_liner_zh: 该文用MD和电子结构计算研究有机笼分子与VEGFR-2蛋白及DNA双界面结合，虽非TF-DNA体系，但涉及蛋白-DNA互作建模，方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: Angiogenesis, driven by vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and its receptor VEGFR-2 domain D2-D3 (VEGFR-2 D23) signaling, plays a central role in tumor vascularization and progression. In this multiscale computational study, we investigate pyrgos[n]cages (PC[n], n = 1-4), purely covalent organic cages with electronically adaptive pi-stacked systems, capable of engaging the extracellular VEGFR-2 D23 ligand-binding interface (wild type and mutant) and DNA (duplex and fork) structures. Molecular dynamics simulations and electronic structure analyses indicate that the electronically soft and polarizable PC[2-4] frameworks preferentially localize within the VEGFR-2 D23 interdomain cleft, stabilized by hydrogen bonding, picdots, three dots, centeredpi stacking, and picdots, three dots, centeredH interactions. This multivalent interaction pattern suggests potential steric interference with VEGF binding while preserving overall receptor structural stability, including mutant VEGFR-2 D23 variants. Complementary DNA-binding analyses reveal structurally stable groove-associated binding stabilized by directional hydrogen bonds, phosphate backbone interactions, picdots, three dots, centeredpi stacking, and van der Waals contacts. Among the studied systems, PC[4] exhibits the most favorable binding enthalpy estimates for VEGFR-2 D23 (-48.3 +/- 3.5 kcal mol(-1)), mutant M-VEGFR-2 D23 (-24.3 +/- 5.8 kcal mol(-1)), and duplex DNA (-44.8 +/- 3.8 kcal mol(-1)). At the same time, PC[2] shows favorable interaction with fork DNA (-46.3 +/- 4.5 kcal mol(-1)). These findings provide mechanistic insight into the organic cage PC[n] in engaging biologically relevant protein-DNA interfaces and highlight its potential to modulate the VEGFR-2 D23 domain and DNA binding.
abstract_zh: 血管内皮生长因子（VEGF）及其受体VEGFR-2结构域D2-D3（VEGFR-2 D23）信号驱动的血管生成，在肿瘤血管化和进展中发挥核心作用。在这项多尺度计算研究中，我们研究了pyrgos[n]cages（PC[n]，n = 1-4），即具有电子适应性π堆叠系统的纯共价有机笼，能够与细胞外VEGFR-2 D23配体结合界面（野生型和突变型）以及DNA（双链和叉状）结构相互作用。分子动力学模拟和电子结构分析表明，电子软且可极化的PC[2-4]框架优先定位于VEGFR-2 D23结构域间裂隙内，通过氢键、π点、三点居中π堆叠以及π点、三点居中H相互作用稳定。这种多价相互作用模式提示对VEGF结合具有潜在的空间干扰，同时保持整体受体结构稳定性，包括突变型VEGFR-2 D23变体。互补的DNA结合分析揭示了结构稳定的沟槽相关结合，由定向氢键、磷酸骨架相互作用、π点、三点居中π堆叠以及范德华接触稳定。在所研究的系统中，PC[4]对VEGFR-2 D23（-48.3 ± 3.5 kcal mol⁻¹）、突变型M-VEGFR-2 D23（-24.3 ± 5.8 kcal mol⁻¹）和双链DNA（-44.8 ± 3.8 kcal mol⁻¹）表现出最有利的结合焓估计。同时，PC[2]对叉状DNA（-46.3 ± 4.5 kcal mol⁻¹）显示出有利的相互作用。这些发现为有机笼PC[n]参与生物学相关蛋白-DNA界面提供了机制性见解，并突显了其调节VEGFR-2 D23结构域和DNA结合的潜力。
